To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the serum levels of homocystine and NO are significantly increased in Alzheimer patients and that the increase of homocystein serum levels correlates with the degree of brain atrophy, as measured by Computed Axia Tomography, in both AD and VD.
Hcy levels are significantly increased in both AD and VD, whereas NO levels are significantly decreased in AD.

1) Hcy levels significantly increased in both AD and VD groups compared with control subjects; 2) NO levels did not change between groups; 3) a significant correlation was found between Hcy levels and brain atrophy, whereas NO levels correlated with atrophy only in AD, not in VD.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of Hcy and of NO in AD and Vascular Dementia, in order to understand the pathogenic mechanisms underlying the disease and the possible use of Hcy and/or NO modulators for the prevention of the disease.
the role played by Hcy and NO in the pathogenesis of dementia and in particular with the effect of both molecules on the brain atrophy.
the role of Hcy and of NO in AD and Vascular Dementia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hcy levels are associated to brain vascular lesion and brain atrophy, while NO levels seem to be protective in AD patients.
both Hcy and NO play a role in the pathophysiology of AD and VD, but with a different effect.
the Hcy/NO system may play an important role in AD and Vascular Dementia pathogenesis, but it may also be useful for a better understanding and treatment of these diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pathogenic effect of Homocytine in AD and Vascular Dementia, and the beneficial effect of nitric oxide in AD, are both associated with specific Computed Axil Tomography findings, and may have a role in the pathogenesis of dementia.

Hcy is a marker of vascular damage, and its increase is related to the severity of brain atrophy, whereas NO is a marker of neurodegenerative damage and its decrease is related to the degree of cognitive impairment in AD.

the Hcy and NO serum levels are significantly increased in AD patients compared to control subjects, independently from the cognitive impairment, and are correlated with brain atrophy in AD and Vascular Dementia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Hcy levels are increased in both dementias, while NO levels are only increased in AD.

the use of CAT in the diagnosis of AD and VD is not only based on the evaluation of the brain atrophy but also on the analysis of the vascular lesion, as a marker of the vascular damage in the AD and VD brain.
homocysteinaemia is associated with brain vascular lesions, independently from dementia subtype.
